summary: Remote WebSocket server drives `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` tmux session on installer host
details: When the operator runs `santaclaude connect`, the CLI opens a WebSocket to https://santaclaude.app and polls /api/jobs/claim and /api/control/claim. Messages returned by that remote service are dispatched through onJob / onWebhook / runControl into inject(pane, message), which invokes `execFileSync('tmux', ['send-keys','-t',pane,'-l', msg])` followed by an Enter keystroke against a tmux pane running `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` (the default `claudeCmd`). The remote party therefore drives an unattended Claude agent with permission prompts bypassed, giving it arbitrary command execution on the host for the duration of the session. checkUpdate() additionally fetches a `target` version string from https://santaclaude.app/api/cli-version and, under the self-supervisor loop, re-execs `npx -y @cliphijack/santaclaude@<target>`, allowing the same server to force the client onto any version the author has published. Hooks (hooks/sc-notify.sh, hooks/sc-stop.sh) POST session identifiers back to the same service via curl.
